parent.title: Pure React 19 SPA or a .NET 10 BFF? A decision framework for an internal admin console

siblings.title: In-memory tokens vs cookie-backed BFF sessions under XSS: what each architecture actually buys you
siblings.summary: httpOnly cookies do not stop XSS — they convert silent token exfiltration into loud, tab-bound session riding. That's a real but bounded win; CSP + Trusted Types is the actual mitigation.

siblings.title: Does the IETF browser-based-apps BCP apply to an internal admin console?
siblings.summary: The BCP names "business applications" in its strongest recommendation, so an internal console is in scope — but the ranking is a security/simplicity trade-off, not a normative MUST.

siblings.title: Greenfield BFF vs retrofitting later: where the asymmetry actually is
siblings.summary: Adding a BFF later is a two-way door — if you build the SPA with one auth module, one fetch wrapper, relative paths and no client-side JWT parsing. The one-way door is the API, not the frontend.

siblings.title: What a BFF costs you every day: OpenAPI codegen and the local dev loop
siblings.summary: A path-preserving BFF leaves OpenAPI codegen essentially untouched — the real daily cost is one extra process, a Vite proxy config, and losing Swagger UI 'Try it out'.

siblings.title: BFF options in .NET 10: Duende.BFF, YARP, or hand-rolled
siblings.summary: If you build a BFF, the realistic .NET 10 choice is YARP + AddOpenIdConnect + the free Apache-2.0 Duende.AccessTokenManagement (~250 LOC you own), or Duende.BFF if you qualify for its free Community Edition; Duende.BFF's paid entry point is $5,750/yr.

sources.title: Privacy Sandbox: next steps
sources.claim: Google announced on 22 Apr 2025 that Chrome will keep third-party cookies and will not ship a standalone choice prompt.

sources.title: AdExchanger: Google isn't launching a user choice prompt
sources.claim: Trade press corroboration of Google's April 2025 reversal on the third-party cookie choice prompt.

sources.title: MDN: Third-party cookies
sources.claim: Per-browser state: Chrome does not block third-party cookies by default; Firefox partitions them via Total Cookie Protection; Safari applies ITP protections by default.

sources.title: WebKit: Full Third-Party Cookie Blocking and More
sources.claim: Safari has blocked all cross-site cookies by default since Safari 13.1 / iOS 13.4 (24 Mar 2020).

sources.title: web.dev: Understanding same-site and same-origin
sources.claim: A 'site' is scheme + registrable domain (eTLD+1); different subdomains of the same registrable domain are same-site.

sources.title: oidc-spa: Third-party cookies and session restoration
sources.claim: Same registrable domain keeps the IdP first-party and lets iframe-based silent session restoration work; cross-site it falls back to a full-page redirect.

sources.title: Keycloak: JavaScript adapter
sources.claim: Session Status iframe and silent check-sso are unsupported when third-party cookies are blocked, and those features may ultimately be deprecated.

sources.title: Skycloak: Keycloak, FedCM and third-party cookie deprecation
sources.claim: keycloak.js silent check-sso and the check-session iframe break under third-party cookie blocking, causing phantom logouts; FedCM in Keycloak 26.x is not production-ready.

sources.title: keycloak#20339: Add support for FedCM
sources.claim: FedCM support in Keycloak is still an open discussion, not a shipped feature.

sources.title: Duende: Third-party cookies
sources.claim: OIDC Session Management and OIDC Silent Login both break under third-party cookie blocking; the BFF replaces them with back-channel logout.

sources.title: Chrome Enterprise: CookiesAllowedForUrls
sources.claim: Chrome Enterprise admins can force third-party cookies to be allowed for specific third-party/top-level site pairs.

sources.title: StatCounter: Browser Market Share Worldwide
sources.claim: Chrome ~65%, Safari ~18%, Edge >5%, Firefox ~3% in 2026.

sources.title: RFC 9700 — OAuth 2.0 Security Best Current Practice
sources.claim: Refresh tokens for public clients MUST be sender-constrained or use refresh token rotation.

sources.title: RFC 9449 — OAuth 2.0 Demonstrating Proof of Possession (DPoP)
sources.claim: Refresh tokens issued to public clients presenting a DPoP proof MUST be bound to that public key.

sources.title: Auth0: Refresh Token Rotation
sources.claim: Reuse detection revokes the entire descendant token family when a used refresh token is replayed.

sources.title: keycloak#16081: rotation + multiple tabs revokes everything
sources.claim: Keycloak's refresh-token rotation revokes all token families for the client when the app is open in multiple tabs; closed as 'not planned'.

sources.title: keycloak#49426: CVE-2026-9802 stale-token check bypass
sources.claim: A server restart resets startupTime and lets previously rotated refresh tokens be redeemed again; fixes targeted at 26.4.13 / 26.6.3 / 26.7.0.

sources.title: Skycloak: Session management in Keycloak
sources.claim: Rotation is configured via 'Revoke Refresh Token' + 'Refresh Token Max Reuse' = 0; defaults 30 min SSO Session Idle, 10 h SSO Session Max.

sources.title: Kévin Chalet: OpenIddict 3.0 beta6
sources.claim: OpenIddict enables rolling refresh tokens by default with a 15-second reuse leeway to survive concurrent refreshes.

sources.title: Keycloak: DPoP support in 26.4
sources.claim: DPoP became officially supported in Keycloak 26.4, including binding only refresh tokens for public clients and dpop_jkt.

sources.title: Keycloak: Securing applications with DPoP
sources.claim: Keycloak documents the per-client 'Require DPoP bound tokens' switch.

sources.title: openiddict-core#2483: DPoP in the validation stack
sources.claim: OpenIddict supports DPoP on issuance but its validation/resource-server stack extracts Bearer tokens only; proof-of-possession is mTLS-only.

sources.title: OpenIddict: Mutual TLS authentication
sources.claim: OpenIddict supports mTLS client authentication and certificate-bound (cnf.x5t#S256) access tokens.

sources.title: InfoQ: DPoP key storage, the unsolved problem
sources.claim: A non-extractable WebCrypto key still leaves a signing oracle reachable from XSS; Firefox cannot persist CryptoKey in IndexedDB; the BFF pattern is the safest browser option today.

sources.title: oidc-client-ts: Demonstrating Proof of Possession
sources.claim: oidc-client-ts implements RFC 9449 with an IndexedDbDPoPStore holding a non-extractable CryptoKeyPair.

sources.title: oidc-spa: DPoP
sources.claim: oidc-spa ships DPoP 'auto' mode with fetch/XHR interceptors; Keycloak 26.4+ supported; Entra ID unsupported.

sources.title: oidc-client-ts#1735: Storage Access API PoC
sources.claim: The Storage Access API workaround requires an explicit user gesture and remains an unmerged proof-of-concept.

sources.title: oidc-client-ts#1032: Does silent renewal using iframes work with modern browsers?
sources.claim: Practitioners report iframe silent renewal failing with opaque console errors, forcing full page reloads.

sources.title: react-oidc-context
sources.claim: React context provider for oidc-client-ts.

sources.title: TanStack Query #7617: token refresh in cache callbacks?
sources.claim: TkDodo advises handling token refresh in an HTTP-layer interceptor rather than QueryCache/MutationCache onError.

sources.title: TanStack Query #6249: async-mutex with axios interceptors
sources.claim: Concurrent queries each hitting 401 fire duplicate refresh calls; the question remains unanswered.

sources.title: TanStack Query: Query Retries
sources.claim: Queries retry 3 times by default with exponential backoff; retry: false disables it.

sources.title: TkDodo: React Query Error Handling
sources.claim: QueryCache global onError fires once per query; useQuery's onError was removed in v5.

sources.title: dev.to: Efficient refresh token implementation with React Query and Axios
sources.claim: The failed-queue (single-flight) pattern is required or simultaneous 401s trigger multiple concurrent refresh calls.

sources.title: Akhila Ariyachandra: Refreshing an authentication token in TanStack Query
sources.claim: Naive interceptors fired the refresh call 6-10 times at once on page reopen.

sources.title: Duende BFF: Session management
sources.claim: A BFF holds tokens server-side and auto-refreshes the access token when close to expiry; needs a session store.
